A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GISL research on gene regulatory network inference under selection bias and latent confounding. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and analyses of Norman, Dixit, and Adamson gene-expression datasets in Section 5 and Appendices G–H.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic comparisons, robustness experiments, and real-data analyses in Section 4 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: v1 Figure 10 and Algorithm 4 distinguish pure selection from causation plus selection using different CI rules. v2 Figure 3 and Algorithm 1 assign both to the same all-dependent selection pattern; Appendix H explicitly says this prevents recovering some causal edges. This substantively changes inference, although the skeleton-discovery, perturbation-testing, and correction framework remains.

E1.justification: Norman, Dixit, and Adamson are retained; the latter two were already evaluated in v1's appendix. Changes concern synthetic scenarios: v2 includes simulated knockdown and a normalized-Hill dynamics test, while v1's explicit selection-free evaluation in Figure 14 is absent.

E2.justification: The principal synthetic comparison replaces PC, GES, and their intervention-refined variants with IGSP, UT-IGSP, and JCI-GSP alongside retained GIES. v2 additionally evaluates CDIS in Table 7 and a collider-identification reference in Table 2. FCI, ICD, PIDC, and PPCOR comparisons remain represented.

E3.justification: Synthetic protocols are substantially revised: v1 sets hard interventions to zero, whereas v2 samples intervention values uniformly; graph-size grids change to 10–25 variables, with additional larger-graph testing and explicit sample-size sweeps. The selection-count experiment changes from 10 to 15 variables. v2 also adds SID evaluation, limits the displayed PAG comparison to precision, and introduces a 0.15 Z-score threshold for quantitative real-data evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond the selection-count sensitivity already present in v1, v2 Table 5 adds explicit tests of noise, edge density, functional complexity, and larger graphs. Figures 6 and 10 add comparisons of Z-score distributions between inferred selection genes and other genes. Conversely, v1's selection-free control testing the benefit of perturbation information is removed.

E5.justification: v1 describes 20 randomly generated graphs per setting and displays uncertainty without clearly defining its reporting convention. v2 specifies 10 independent graphs or seeded runs for the revised experiments, identifies Figure 4 error bars as 95% confidence intervals, and describes table summaries as means and variances. This changes replication and uncertainty documentation, without establishing increased replication.

E6.justification: v2 replaces substantial synthetic results and adds SID, robustness, and CDIS results. Corresponding computational-baseline tables also change: PIDC's reported Acc goes from 21.6 to 51.6 and PPCOR's from 17.4 to 43.4 in v1 Table 2 versus v2 Table 6. New real-data proxy accuracies are 77.7% on Dixit, 80.2% on Adamson, and 74.8% on Norman. These reported changes do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1's separate identifiability theorems and Appendix F proofs are replaced by Theorem 3.7 and Appendix D. The unique-recovery guarantee without latent confounders is dropped, and v1's restriction excluding latent ancestors of selection variables is no longer stated. Selection-related CI reasoning is substantively reversed in Remark 3.4, and the guarantee is reformulated around four CI-pattern classes.

C1.justification: v2 makes generality without additional graphical assumptions beyond standard assumptions an explicit contribution, whereas v1's introduction qualifies identification by mild graphical conditions and its theorem imposes an additional restriction. The identification claim is redefined around four CI-pattern equivalence classes, replacing the separate exact and restricted partial-identification claims. The central selection-bias motivation and GISL contribution remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains missed causal edges through the indistinguishability of pure selection and causation plus selection, and interprets precision–recall tradeoffs accordingly. It qualifies high Z-scores as necessary supporting evidence rather than sufficient identification of selection pairs. Appendices E–H also expand explanations of persistent selection versus CDIS, biological constraints, and the difficulty of reliable selection detection.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies KCI with alpha 0.05, provides a runtime example of approximately ten minutes on one CPU core, adds a GISL code link, and details the Z-score calculation in Appendix G. These are useful documentation additions. Code availability remains internally inconsistent: Appendix E says code is available, while the checklist says it will be released after review.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated related-work appendix covering GRNI method families, confounded and selection-biased causal discovery, and interventional approaches. It substantively positions GISL against parametric restrictions, FCI-based equivalence classes, JCI, and CDIS, with numerous additional cited works. This extends research positioning well beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the separate GISB/GISL and identifiability sections are reorganized into a unified GISL methodology section. Experiments are restructured around selection detection, regulatory recovery, and real-data evidence. Appendices are extensively reorganized, with new related-work and explanatory sections and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redraws intervention and CI diagrams, replaces the benchmark plot grids with sample-size-faceted displays, and adds robustness, SID, and comparison tables plus grouped Z-score plots. Gene-network figures are redrawn and relocated. Some material is retained and moved, including the PPCOR network and individual-gene Z-score plots. The overall document format also changes.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable intervention-aware comparisons, robustness tests, clearer uncertainty reporting, and substantially improved exposition. However, its central theoretical revision introduces an unresolved tension: Remark 3.4 explicitly says the selection CI behavior violates Markov and faithfulness assumptions, while Theorem 3.7 relies on those assumptions for its broadened guarantee. The PDFs do not reconcile this mismatch. The empirical and presentation gains coexist with uncertainty affecting the main method's justification, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
